title: Monkey raids cost farmers millions annually: Study - The Rising Nepal
description: Monkey raids cost farmers millions annually: Study  The Rising Nepal
publisher.title: The Rising Nepal
full_article:
Kathmandu, Aug. 11: Growing conflicts with wild animals -- monkeys, wild boars and porcupines -- have emerged as a serious threat to agriculture and rural livelihoods in the country’s mid-hills, with rhesus macaques (species of moneky) alone causing an estimated Rs. 50 million in crop losses every year.

A study was conducted by the National Trust for Nature Conservation (NTNC) with the technical support by Central Department of Zoology, TU across 44 highly affected local units (18 municipalities and 26 rural municipalities) of Gandaki, Bagmati, Karnali, Koshi and Sudurpaschim. The study found that corn was most affected crop among cultivated crops.

According to the report, with over 104,000 monkeys roaming forest margins near agricultural fields, farming communities are suffering tens of millions of rupees in annual damages. Farmers regularly lose over 50 per cent of their annual maize production to troops of monkeys, alongside substantial destruction of rice, wheat, potatoes, and high-value cash crops like cardamom, the report said.

Monkeys alone cause an estimated annual loss of Rs. 50 million across surveyed farms. Corn is hardest hit, with farmers losing an average of 312 kg per year -- over 50 per cent of total production -- totaling Rs. 25 million in losses for maize alone.

Regional hotspots show catastrophic loss rates, including 90 per cent corn loss in Gandaki, 88 per cent corn loss in Karnali, and 85 to 90 per cent losses for rice and wheat in Sudurpaschim.

Despair among rural communities has reduced traditional deterrents -- such as shouting, using dogs, or throwing stones -- largely ineffective. In response, nearly 70 per cent of surveyed farmers believe controlled culling is the only permanent solution.

Out of frustration, locals have turned to high-voltage electrocution traps, mass drowning in lethal ponds and unsanctioned translocations. These actions explicitly violate Nepal’s National Parks and Wildlife Conservation Act, 1973, posing severe risks to human life, causing animal cruelty, and failing to offer a long-term solution, the report said.

The report also said that standard government relief efforts remain out of reach, as 80 per cent of affected farmers report being unaware of available compensation funds. Rachana Shah, spokesperson at NTNC, said that amidst growing human-wildlife friction, local communities are urgently calling for the active management and relocation of monkeys from their settlements.

“Residents are demanding that the government deploy modern technologies and population control measures to address the issue. They are in favor of a range of solutions, including relocating the primates to other areas, implementing fertility control and along with other globally practiced population management tools,” she said.

She said the main objective of the study was to assess the economic loss and implement sustainable strategies to mitigate human-monkey, porcupine-wild boar conflicts, ensuring the safety and well-being of both humans and wildlife.

It was also to identify the population of monkeys, mainly rhesus macaque, wild boar and porcupine, she said.

The study made various recommendations including establish a National Rhesus Macaque Management Task Force under the Ministry of Agriculture, Forests and Environment.

The task force needs to develop a national strategy ensuring coordination among federal, provincial, and local governments, academia, conservation organizations, and community forest user groups. So a priority area for monkey management will be developed after combining habitat management, community-based deterrence, selective sterilization, compensation mechanisms, and regulated culling.

It also suggested to promote plantation of monkey-preferred fruit species within forests and away from farmlands, establish buffer zones and green corridors between forests and agricultural areas, and regulate waste disposal and strictly discourage deliberate feeding near settlements, roads, and religious sites.

The study was conducted utilizing field visits, stakeholder consultations, GIS mapping, and a survey of 1,846 households.

full_article:
KATHMANDU, AUGUST 11

Rain and thundershowers are likely in parts of Nepal on Tuesday, with the Himalayan and hilly regions expected to remain generally cloudy while conditions in the Terai will be partly cloudy, according to the Meteorological Forecasting Division.

Moderate rain or snowfall accompanied by thunder and lightning is likely at a few places in the Himalayan region, while some parts of the hilly regions may receive moderate rainfall with thunderstorms.

One or two places in the Terai regions are also likely to receive moderate rainfall.

The weather is expected to remain broadly similar tonight, with cloudy conditions continuing across the Himalayan and hilly regions and partly cloudy skies in the Terai. Moderate rain or snowfall is possible at a few places in the Himalayan and hilly regions, while one or two places in the Terai may receive moderate rain.

Pokhara, Kathmandu among wetter cities

Pokhara is forecast to receive moderate rain with thundershowers today, with a 60 percent chance of rain and a maximum temperature of 29–31°C. The chance of rain rises to 70 percent tonight, when temperatures are expected to fall to 21–23°C.

In Kathmandu, light rain with thunderstorms is likely during the day, with a 40 percent chance of rain and a maximum temperature of 29–31°C. The capital could see moderate rain with thundershowers at night, with the probability rising to 60 percent.

Okhaldhunga, Dhankuta, Jiri and Taplejung are also expected to receive moderate rain with thundershowers during the day.

Meanwhile, parts of the southern plains are likely to remain comparatively drier. Nepalgunj, Bhairahawa, Simara and Janakpur are forecast to remain partly cloudy during the day, with no rainfall currently forecast for those cities.

The highest daytime temperatures among the listed cities are expected to reach 34–36°C in Bhairahawa, Simara, Biratnagar and Janakpur.

Monsoon remains active

The weather office said the entire country remains under the influence of monsoon winds, while the monsoon trough is currently positioned around its average location.

The forecast indicates that rainfall will remain concentrated mainly over the Himalayan and hilly regions, although isolated moderate showers are also possible in the Terai.

काठमाण्डू, ११ अगस्त

मौसम पूर्वानुमान प्रभाग के अनुसार मंगलदिन नेपाल के कुछ हिस्सा में वर्षा आ गरज के संभावना अछि, हिमालय आ पहाड़ी क्षेत्र में सामान्यतः बादल छाएत रहबाक संभावना अछि जखन कि तराई के हालत आंशिक रूप सं बादल छाएत रहत।

संबंधित लेख पहाड़ी आ पहाड़क पार गरजबाक संभावना; आंशिक बादल केरऽ आवरण के बावजूद भी भारी बारिश के खतरा बनलऽ छै बारिश, पहाड़ी आरू हिमालयी क्षेत्रऽ में गरजऽ के संभावना; तराई मे गर्मी के लहर जारी अछि

हिमालय क्षेत्र केरऽ कुछ जगहऽ प॑ मध्यम बारिश या गरज आरू बिजली के साथ बर्फबारी के संभावना छै, जबकि पहाड़ी क्षेत्रऽ के कुछ हिस्सा म॑ ठनका के साथ मध्यम वर्षा होय सकै छै ।

तराई क्षेत्र मे एक-दू ठाम सेहो मध्यम वर्षा हेबाक संभावना अछि।

आइ राति मौसम मोटा-मोटी समान रहबाक संभावना अछि, हिमालय आ पहाड़ी क्षेत्र मे बादल छाएत आ तराई मे आंशिक रूप सँ बादल छाएत। हिमालय आ पहाड़ी क्षेत्र मे किछु ठाम मध्यम वर्षा या बर्फबारी संभव अछि, जखन कि तराई मे एक या दू ठाम मध्यम वर्षा भ सकैत अछि ।

पोखरा, काठमांडू आर्द्र शहर के बीच

पोखरा म॑ आय गरज के साथ मध्यम बारिश के अनुमान छै, जेकरा म॑ बारिश के ६० प्रतिशत संभावना आरू अधिकतम तापमान २९-३१ डिग्री सेल्सियस के अनुमान छै । आइ राति बरखा के संभावना 70 प्रतिशत भ गेल अछि, जखन कि तापमान 21-23 डिग्री सेल्सियस तक गिरय के उम्मीद अछि.

काठमांडू में दिन में गरज के साथ हल्का बारिश के संभावना छै, जेकरा में बारिश के 40 प्रतिशत संभावना आरू अधिकतम तापमान 29–31 डिग्री सेल्सियस के संभावना छै । राजधानी मे राति मे गरज के संग मध्यम बरखा भ सकैत अछि, जेकर संभावना 60 प्रतिशत तक बढ़ि सकैत अछि।

ओखलढुंगा, धनकुटा, जिरी आ ताप्लेजुङ मे सेहो दिन मे ठनका के संग मध्यम वर्षा के संभावना अछि ।

एम्हर दक्षिणी मैदानक किछु भाग अपेक्षाकृत शुष्क रहबाक संभावना अछि । नेपालगंज, भैरहवा, सिमरा आ जनकपुरमे दिनमे आंशिक रूपसँ बादल छाएत रहबाक अनुमान अछि, अखन ओहि शहरमे वर्षा नै हेबाक अनुमान अछि ।

title: LPG Gas Supply Disruption in Nepal Due to Hoarding Despite Increased Imports - Ratopati
description: LPG Gas Supply Disruption in Nepal Due to Hoarding Despite Increased Imports  Ratopati
publisher.title: Ratopati
full_article:
Kathmandu. The import and supply of cooking gas (LPG) in Nepal are exceeding normal levels. However, an artificial shortage is being observed in the market.

According to Nepal Oil Corporation and gas industrialists, the supply system is facing problems due to consumers unnecessarily hoarding cylinders, even though imports are higher than the daily demand.

According to Gokul Bhandari, Managing Director of Nepal Gas Industries Pvt. Ltd., Nepal's normal monthly consumption is around 3.5 million cylinders. Based on this, the daily demand is about 110,000 cylinders.

However, current data shows that Nepal Oil Corporation is importing gas equivalent to 130,000 cylinders daily. Despite sending 20,000 more cylinders than regular consumption to the market, the market has not stabilized due to psychological fear among consumers and hoarding tendencies.

“Although a decision was made earlier to go with half cylinders of 7 kg, its implementation was delayed by four months due to various reasons,” said Managing Director Bhandari. “During this period, about 30,000 metric tons, equivalent to 2.1 million cylinders, of gas were imported less.

However, with consumption remaining the same, the cylinders in consumers' homes started depleting.” He analyzes that the current demand has increased unusually because refilling 14.2 kg cylinders became necessary after returning to the previous system.

Currently, there are 17.5 million cylinders in the market. This number is sufficient to meet Nepal's total consumption for five months. However, not all these cylinders are with the industries; they are in consumers' homes, either empty or half-filled. Only 40 percent of the total population uses gas. But due to hoarding tendencies, students and low-income groups are suffering the most.

Some consumers and retailers are unnecessarily hoarding gas. In the lines formed in areas like Balaju in Kathmandu, many people wanting to keep unnecessary stock were seen, more than consumers who were genuinely in trouble. It was also found that the same person was queuing up multiple times.

To streamline the supply system, industrialists have started daily reporting. Details of how much each industry imported and to which dealer how much gas was sent are being provided to Nepal Oil Corporation.

The government has now directed to keep records of which retailer sold gas to which customer. Businessmen have stated that the implementation process for this has begun. This is expected to ensure equitable distribution of gas and prevent black marketing.

Industrialists state that the current problem is not due to a decrease in gas imports but because consumers are trying to stock up. “In a place where 110,000 cylinders are consumed daily, 130,000 are arriving,” Bhandari said. “Therefore, if those who have 15 days to one month's gas stock at home do not take additional gas immediately, consumers who genuinely need it will be able to get gas easily.”

He clarified that the current situation is not like the time of the blockade or COVID-19 and urged not to hoard unnecessarily.

Meanwhile, due to the lack of concrete laws related to petroleum and explosives in Nepal, gas industries are compelled to operate based on foreign standards. So far, Nepal has not enacted its own Explosives Act or Petroleum Act. Domestic gas industries are established and operated based on the certification of Indian bodies and Indian laws.

Bhandari, who is also the Vice President of the Confederation of Nepalese Industries, said, “The legal and policy structure to regulate the LPG industry in Nepal is still weak. Industries are operating after being certified by Indian standards.”

He pointed out the need for clear laws and an effective state mechanism for the industry's safety, monitoring, and regulation.

There also appears to be a need to review the subsidy provided on gas. Currently, the state is incurring a loss of approximately 900 rupees per cylinder of gas. However, there has been no clear classification on which group should receive the concession. Currently, the same price is set for both commercial and domestic purposes.

“Currently, even the commercial sector is getting relatively cheaper gas and taking advantage of VAT refunds,” Bhandari said. “A policy of providing subsidies only to the targeted group, rather than to everyone equally, seems necessary. The system needs to be improved so that subsidies reach the actual targeted consumers.”

For a long-term solution, industrialists say that the state and private sectors need to collaborate on storage infrastructure, improvement of the distribution system, and pipeline construction. Since gas is an essential commodity and the private sector has 100 percent investment in it, the state's role is crucial in managing it. Bhandari stated that to increase gas storage capacity, similar to petroleum products, a public-private partnership (PPP) model should be adopted.

Nepal Oil Corporation is moving forward with discussions with Indian Oil Corporation regarding pipeline expansion. Businessmen believe that with such infrastructure development, many of the problems related to LPG supply and distribution can be resolved. They said that by maintaining sufficient stock during times of easy supply, future shortages can be avoided.

काठमांडू। नेपाल मे कुकिंग गैस (एलपीजी) के आयात आ आपूर्ति सामान्य स्तर स बेसी भ रहल अछि। मुदा बाजार मे कृत्रिम कमी देखल जा रहल अछि।

नेपाल तेल निगम आ गैस उद्योगपतिसबके अनुसार उपभोक्ताके सिलेण्डरके अनावश्यक जमाखोरीके कारण सप्लाई व्यवस्थामे समस्याके सामना करल रहै, भले ही आयात दैनिक माँगसे अधिक हो ।

नेपाल गैस इण्डस्ट्रीज प्रा.लि.के प्रबन्धनिदेशक गोकुल भण्डारीके अनुसार । लिमिटेड, नेपालक सामान्य मासिक खपत लगभग ३५ लाख सिलेंडर अछि । एकर आधार पर रोजाना करीब एक लाख 10 हजार सिलेंडर क मांग अछि।

मुदा वर्तमान आंकड़ा बता रहल अछि जे नेपाल तेल निगम प्रतिदिन एक लाख तीस हजार सिलेंडर के बराबर गैस आयात क रहल अछि। नियमित खपत स 20 हजार बेसी सिलेंडर बाजार मे भेजला क बावजूद उपभोक्ता मे मनोवैज्ञानिक डर आ जमाखोरी क प्रवृत्ति क कारण बाजार स्थिर नहि भ सकल अछि।

प्रबंध निदेशक भंडारी कहलनि जे, हालांकि पहिने 7 किलो के हाफ सिलेंडर के संग जेबाक निर्णय लेल गेल छल, मुदा विभिन्न कारण सं एकर क्रियान्वयन मे चारि मासक देरी भेल। ओ कहला जे एहि दौरान करीब 30 हजार मीट्रिक टन गैस क आयात कम भेल, जे 21 लाख सिलेंडर क बराबर अछि।

मुदा, खपत ओहिना रहला स उपभोक्ता घर मे सिलेंडर खतम होबय लागल।” हुनकऽ विश्लेषण छै कि वर्तमान मांग असामान्य रूप स॑ बढ़ी गेलऽ छै, कैन्हेंकि पिछला सिस्टम म॑ वापसी के बाद १४.२ किलो के सिलेंडर क॑ रिफिल करना जरूरी होय गेलऽ छेलै ।

फिलहाल बाजार मे 1.75 करोड़ सिलेंडर अछि। ई संख्या पाँच मासक लेल नेपालक कुल खपत पूरा करबाक लेल पर्याप्त अछि । मुदा, ई सब सिलेंडर उद्योग सबहक संग नहिं छैक; उपभोक्ता कें घर मे छै, या त खाली या आधा भरल. कुल आबादी मे मात्र 40 प्रतिशत गैस क उपयोग करैत अछि। मुदा जमाखोरी के प्रवृत्ति के कारण सबस बेसी नुकसान छात्र आ कम आय वाला समूह के भ रहल अछि.

किछु उपभोक्ता आ खुदरा विक्रेता अनावश्यक रूप स गैस जमा क रहल छथि। काठमांडू के बालाजू सन इलाका मे बनल लाइन मे अनावश्यक स्टॉक राखय चाहय वाला बहुत लोक देखल गेल, ओहि उपभोक्ता सं बेसि जे सही मायने मे परेशानी मे पड़ल छल. इहो पता चलल जे एकहि व्यक्ति कई बेर कतार मे ठाढ़ छल।

आपूर्ति प्रणाली कए सुव्यवस्थित करबा लेल उद्योगपति रोज रिपोर्टिंग शुरू करि देलथि अछि। प्रत्येक उद्योग कतेक आयात केलक आ कोन डीलर के कतेक गैस पठाओल गेल तकर विवरण नेपाल तेल निगम के उपलब्ध कराओल जा रहल अछि ।

सरकार आब निर्देश देलक अछि जे कोन खुदरा विक्रेता कोन ग्राहक कए गैस बेचलक। व्यवसायी सब के कहनाय छनि जे एकरा लागू करय के प्रक्रिया शुरू भ गेल अछि. एहि स गैस क समान वितरण सुनिश्चित करबाक आ ब्लैक मार्केटिंग कए रोकबाक उम्मीद अछि।

उद्योगपति सब के कहनाय छनि जे वर्तमान समस्या गैस के आयात में कमी के कारण नहिं बल्कि उपभोक्ता के स्टॉक करय के कोशिश के कारण अछि. भंडारी कहला जे जाहि ठाम रोज एक लाख 10 हजार सिलेंडर क खपत भ रहल अछि, ओहि ठाम एक लाख 30 हजार सिलेंडर आबि रहल अछि। “अतः जिनका घर मे 15 दिन स एक महीना क गैस स्टॉक अछि ओ अगर तुरंत अतिरिक्त गैस नहि लेत त जे उपभोक्ता कए एकर सही मायने मे जरूरत अछि, ओकरा गैस आसानी स भेट सकैत अछि।”

ओ स्पष्ट केलनि जे वर्तमान स्थिति नाकाबंदी या कोविड-19 के समय जेकाँ नहि अछि आ अनावश्यक जमाखोरी नहि करबाक आग्रह केलनि।

एम्हर नेपाल मे पेट्रोलियम आ विस्फोटक स संबंधित ठोस कानून नहि रहला स गैस उद्योग विदेशी मानक क आधार पर संचालित करबा लेल बाध्य अछि। एखन धरि नेपाल अपन विस्फोटक अधिनियम वा पेट्रोलियम कानून नहि बनौलक अछि । घरेलू गैस उद्योगक कें स्थापना आ संचालन भारतीय निकाय आ भारतीय कानून कें प्रमाणीकरण कें आधार पर कैल जायत छै.

नेपाली उद्योग महासंघक उपाध्यक्ष सेहो रहल भंडारी कहलनि जे, “नेपाल मे एलपीजी उद्योग केँ नियमन करबाक लेल कानूनी आ नीतिगत संरचना एखनो कमजोर अछि।उद्योग भारतीय मानक सँ प्रमाणित भेलाक बाद संचालित भ’ रहल अछि।”

हुनी उद्योग के सुरक्षा, निगरानी, ​​आरू नियमन लेली स्पष्ट कानून आरू प्रभावी राज्य तंत्र के जरूरत के ओर इशारा करलकै ।

गैस पर देल गेल सब्सिडी क समीक्षा करबाक सेहो जरूरत देखा रहल अछि। फिलहाल राज्य कए गैस क प्रति सिलेंडर लगभग 900 टका क नुकसान भ रहल अछि। मुदा एहि पर कोनो स्पष्ट वर्गीकरण नहि भेल अछि जे कोन समूह कए इ रियायत भेटबाक चाही। फिलहाल व्यावसायिक आ घरेलू दुनू काज लेल एकहि दाम तय कैल गेल अछि।

भण्डारी कहला जे फिलहाल वाणिज्यिक क्षेत्र मे सेहो गैस अपेक्षाकृत सस्ता भ रहल अछि आ वैट वापसी क फायदा उठा रहल अछि। “सब्सिडी सब्सिडी देबय के नीति सब के समान रूप स नै बल्कि केवल लक्षित समूह के देबय के नीति जरूरी बुझाइत अछि।सिस्टम में सुधार के जरूरत अछि ताकि सब्सिडी वास्तविक लक्षित उपभोक्ता तक पहुंचय।”

दीर्घकालिक समाधान कें लेल उद्योगपतिक कें कहनाय छै कि राज्य आ निजी क्षेत्रक कें भंडारण बुनियादी ढाँचा, वितरण प्रणाली मे सुधार, आ पाइपलाइन निर्माण पर सहयोग करय कें जरूरत छै. चूँकि गैस एकटा आवश्यक वस्तु अछि आ निजी क्षेत्र कए एहि मे शत-प्रतिशत निवेश अछि, एहि लेल एकर प्रबंधन मे राज्य क भूमिका बहुत महत्वपूर्ण अछि। भंडारी नँ कहलकै कि पेट्रोलियम उत्पाद के समान गैस भंडारण क्षमता बढ़ाबै लेली सार्वजनिक-निजी साझेदारी (पीपीपी) मॉडल अपनाबै के चाही ।

नेपाल तेल निगम पाइपलाइन विस्तार के संबंध मे भारतीय तेल निगम के संग चर्चा के संग आगू बढ़ि रहल अछि। व्यवसायी के मानब छै कि एहि तरहक बुनियादी ढांचा के विकास सं एलपीजी के आपूर्ति आ वितरण सं जुड़ल बहुत रास समस्या के समाधान भ सकैत अछि. ओ सब कहला जे आसान आपूर्ति क समय मे पर्याप्त स्टॉक रखला स भविष्य मे कमी स बचल जा सकैत अछि।

KATHMANDU, AUGUST 11

Cimex Inc, the authorised distributor and service provider of BYD vehicles in Nepal, has launched a nationwide customer care campaign aimed at enhancing after-sales services, vehicle connectivity and ownership protection for existing customers.

The "BYD Update to Care+" campaign was inaugurated at Cimex Care, the BYD service centre in Guheshwori, and is now available across the company's 13 service centres nationwide.

Under the campaign, eligible BYD vehicles delivered before September 2024 that did not previously have connected-car features will receive complimentary BYD App connectivity and infotainment activation.

title: Sher Bahadur Deuba Returns to Nepal After Medical Treatment - Ratopati
description: Sher Bahadur Deuba Returns to Nepal After Medical Treatment  Ratopati
publisher.title: Ratopati
full_article:
Kathmandu. Top leaders of the Nepali Congress will arrive at Tribhuvan International Airport to welcome former party president Sher Bahadur Deuba, who is scheduled to return to the country on Thursday after medical treatment.

Leader Min Bishwakarma informed that top leaders will go to the airport to welcome Deuba under the leadership of Dr. Shashank Koirala, coordinator of the National Gathering Preparation Committee, which the Nepali Congress's establishment- इतर (former president Deuba and Dr. Shekhar Koirala) group is organizing in Kathmandu from Shrawan 29.

'Top leaders will go to the airport under the leadership of Dr. Shashank Koirala, coordinator of the National Gathering Organizing Committee, to welcome him (Deuba),' Bishwakarma told Ratopati. 'A large group including former acting president Purna Bahadur Khadka, leader Dr. Shekhar Koirala, former office bearers, and central members will go to the airport to welcome him.'

According to Bishwakarma, Deuba is scheduled to land at Tribhuvan International Airport at 12 PM on Thursday via Thai Air from Thailand. The इतर group of Congress has made preparations to give a grand welcome to leader Deuba, who is returning to the country after a long period of treatment.

Deuba, who left Nepal for medical treatment in Singapore on February 13, reached Hong Kong on March 7 for further treatment after completing his treatment there. Bishwakarma informed that Deuba's program was to go to Thailand from Hong Kong and return to Nepal from Thailand.

On August 24, during the 'Gen Z' movement, protestors severely beat Deuba couple at their residence in Budhanilkantha, leaving them near death. After a long treatment at the Military Hospital in Chhauni, Deuba couple went to Singapore for further treatment.

His family sources have been stating that Deuba has been undergoing treatment abroad for a long time due to health complications arising from the same incident.

Leaders have said that Deuba will be active in the party's internal activities immediately after returning to the country. Bishwakarma, coordinator of the publicity committee, confirmed that former Prime Minister Deuba is scheduled to address the national gathering organized by the इतर group in Kathmandu from Shrawan 29 to 31.

The dispute that emerged after the special general convention in the last week of Poush within Congress has reached its peak. Leaders are publicizing that Deuba will address the national gathering organized by the इतर group amidst that dispute.

title: The distant dream: How administrative negligence jeopardises Nepali football - The Himalayan Times
description: The distant dream: How administrative negligence jeopardises Nepali football  The Himalayan Times
publisher.title: The Himalayan Times
full_article:
Another FIFA World Cup came to a close, demonstrating the absolute pinnacle of international football. Despite the global spectacle, fans of nations that missed qualification felt a common void. Nepal was no exception. The current administrative negligence of Nepali sports only makes the dream seem more distant.

ANFA's governance issues-mismanagement, the absence of dedicated leaders, and political infighting-take a direct toll on national players' ability to perform at their full potential. Almost 60 days have passed since FIFA imposed a ban on ANFA on account of its failure to fulfill eligibility criteria. Yet, no informed actions or strategic decisions have been taken to mitigate the consequences. Consequently, the future of Nepali sports and athletes remains in limbo.

Related Articles FIFA suspends ANFA with immediate effect, bars Nepal from international football The Wildest FIFA World Cup Debate Begins ft. Niti Shah & Rabin Shrestha | Xtreme Football Circus

An athlete's prime career span is roughly eight to ten years. A two-year ban and stalled leagues consume a significant portion of their active careers, effectively stifling their progress. Echoing the reality of leaders on the pitch, Nepali national team central midfielder Sumit Shrestha noted, "As players, our primary focus is always on football. We hope the situation is resolved soon so that we can concentrate on the game and our future." Zero scouting and narrow possibilities of international exposure have led to dire consequences. This has significantly exacerbated the number of players leaving the country seeking better opportunities abroad. There has been a drastic surge in potential athletes opting for non-sporting jobs for financial security and long-term stability over uncertain domestic futures.

This institutional failure has a ripple effect on every entity within the ecosystem: local clubs, academies, and grassroots youth programs all face a steep decline in their overall growth and functioning. The places where young talents are recognized and fostered now lack direction, like a ship with nowhere to land. The absence of local heroes to look up to disrupts the chain of inspiration for current and future generations-a lack of trailblazers and inspiring stories takes a heavy toll on budding athletes. Additionally, the psychological strain that players endure-having spent their entire youth training for a career that administrative politics froze overnight-cannot be overlooked. Giving a lifetime to a dream, having everything it takes to bring it to life, only to be obstructed by circumstances beyond their control feels like a profound act of injustice.

title: Nepal’s para swimmers chase Asian Games glory despite lack of facilities - Khabarhub
description: Nepal’s para swimmers chase Asian Games glory despite lack of facilities  Khabarhub
publisher.title: Khabarhub
full_article:
KATHMANDU: Swimming requires water, but for para swimmers, getting into the pool is only the beginning.

Regular training, accessible infrastructure, qualified coaches, physiotherapy, recovery facilities, nutrition, transportation and financial support are equally important.

Nepal’s para swimmers, however, are preparing for international competition amid a shortage of many of these basic facilities. Despite limited resources and difficult circumstances, they are training with the dream of flying Nepal’s flag high at the upcoming Para Asian Games.

Nepal has been participating in the Para Asian Games since 2010. However, its achievement at the continental event remains limited.

So far, Nepal has won only one medal at the Para Asian Games — a bronze secured by taekwondo athlete Palesha Goverdhan in the under-56 kg category at the 19th Asian Para Games in 2023.

Nepal’s para swimming team now hopes to add a new chapter to that history.

Training continues despite challenges

Under the Nepal Para Swimming Association, head coach Subas Shrestha has been providing regular training to four athletes — Srijana Sarki, Jenisha Kathayat, Harkaman Gharti and Member Singi Syangbo.

The athletes have been training regularly for the past five to six months.

According to coach Shrestha, the athletes have shown good commitment during training. However, a shortage of resources and facilities has made it difficult to take their preparations to the desired level.

Access to a swimming pool itself had been a major challenge. Training has become somewhat easier after Refresh Recreation Centre made its swimming pool and lanes available at a concessional rate.

But the challenges extend beyond the pool.

Physiotherapy, recovery facilities, jacuzzi services, nutrition, transportation and specialised sporting equipment remain difficult to arrange for the athletes.

For Shrestha, the biggest challenge is preparing the athletes for international-level competition with limited resources.

The athletes have talent and determination, he says, but inadequate facilities make it difficult for them to prepare according to their full potential.

Yet, their confidence and commitment continue to drive the team forward.

Srijana’s first international dream

For 19-year-old Srijana Sarki, swimming is more than a sport. It is also a way of proving herself.

Sarki, originally from Jumla in Karnali Province, saw her life change three years ago after she was buried in a landslide while digging soil. The accident left her living with a disability and brought a series of challenges.

But she refused to give up on her dreams.

Currently preparing for undergraduate studies while living in Gokarneshwor, Sarki regularly travels to her training venue. Sometimes she takes a taxi and sometimes a tempo to reach practice.

She has been putting particular focus on swimming for the past three months.

The upcoming competition will be her first international event.

She is excited about getting the opportunity to represent Nepal for the first time and is determined to perform to the best of her ability and compete for a medal.

For Sarki, simply reaching an international competition is already a major achievement.

But she does not want to limit herself to participation.

When she enters the water, she wants her ability — rather than the pain of her past — to define her.

Harkaman: From losing both hands to finding identity in swimming

The story of 21-year-old Harkaman Gharti of Baglung is also one of extraordinary resilience.

Eleven years ago, electricity was connected to his village for the first time. During the process, Gharti suffered an electric shock after touching a main insulator.

The accident resulted in the loss of both his hands.

But the physical loss did not diminish his determination to compete in sport.

Gharti has been active in domestic sports for the past six years and now hopes to prove his ability at the international level through swimming.

A year ago, he obtained an international athlete licence in Japan.

However, he continues to face a shortage of essential recovery facilities, including jacuzzi services and physiotherapy.

Because of these limitations, Gharti says he cannot guarantee a medal at the upcoming competition.

His ambitions, however, extend beyond a single medal.

He wants to accumulate the necessary experience and qualification standards to compete at future Olympic and World Championship events.

For Gharti, swimming is not simply about competition. It has become a way to introduce himself to the world on his own terms.

Jenisha gets another chance

For Jenisha Kathayat from Sudurpaschim Province, swimming is not a new journey.

She has been involved in the sport for nine years.

While studying in Grade 10, she lost a leg. Yet she did not give up swimming. Instead, she turned the challenge into motivation and made the sport part of her identity.

Kathayat has already represented Nepal at the 19th Asian Games in China.

She could not deliver the performance she had hoped for at the event, but the experience did not weaken her confidence.

Instead, it strengthened her determination to return better prepared.

While continuing her higher education, Kathayat has also maintained her focus on training.

This time, she wants to turn her previous international experience into an improved performance.

Her target is clear — a medal.

Member Singi: From an accident to the swimming lane

Among the four athletes, Member Singi Syangbo’s journey from a road accident to the swimming pool is equally remarkable.

At the age of 17, Syangbo was involved in a road accident near the Rasuwagadhi border with China.

He had been working as a helper on a Nepali container truck and had travelled to China while learning to drive and gaining experience.

While waiting for his turn at the border, another vehicle suddenly struck him.

The accident resulted in the loss of one of his legs.

Life was not easy after the accident.

While arranging for a prosthetic leg, however, Syangbo came into contact with swimming.

He had never planned to become a swimmer.

After getting an opportunity, he entered the pool with little more than the thought of giving it a try.

Gradually, swimming became an important part of his life.

Now 26, Syangbo trains every day. He has been undergoing regular training for around two months and says his preparations are progressing well.

Swimming is no longer simply a way to spend time.

His ambitions changed after he began competing.

“Bringing home a medal” is now his clear objective.

Syangbo believes Nepal has a good chance of winning a medal in para swimming this time and continues to train with that goal.

Although the relevant organisations have provided some assistance with training and daily expenses, he says not all the facilities required for high-level preparation are available.

His confidence, however, remains strong.

Four athletes, one goal

Srijana is preparing for her first international competition.

Jenisha wants to improve on her previous international performance.

Harkaman has his sights set on the qualification pathway for future Olympics and World Championships.

Member Singi wants to win a medal at his first major international opportunity.

Their stories are different.

One was left with a disability after a landslide. Another lost both hands in an electrical accident. Another lost a leg during adolescence. The fourth lost a leg in a road accident.

But they share one thing — an unwavering determination to compete.

Their biggest challenge remains the shortage of facilities.

There is limited funding, inadequate accessible sports infrastructure and insufficient access to physiotherapy, recovery facilities, equipment and nutrition.

Even reaching the training venue can require a personal struggle.

Yet, once they enter the pool, those difficulties are temporarily pushed aside.

In the swimming lane, they focus on their abilities rather than their physical conditions. Every stroke is an attempt to improve their time, and every training session brings them closer to their dream of performing on the international stage.

A coach’s challenge

For head coach Subas Shrestha, the four athletes are not merely competitors. They are athletes with significant potential.

Their determination and work ethic are strong, but competing internationally requires regular and scientific training.

That requires time, equipment, facilities and financial resources.

Preparing athletes with limited resources remains a major challenge for Shrestha, but their potential continues to motivate him.

His approach is to focus on the athletes’ abilities rather than their limitations, making the best possible use of available resources to improve their technique, timing and performance.

However, if Nepal wants to target international medals, he believes their preparation needs to become more systematic and long-term.

Dreams in the water

Nepal’s para-sports sector still has a long way to go.

A single medal cannot transform the sporting landscape. Sustained investment, infrastructure, training and long-term support for athletes are necessary.

For now, four athletes are searching for their future in the swimming pool.

Srijana wants to prove herself on her first international journey.

Harkaman wants to take his sporting career towards the Olympics and World Championships.

Jenisha hopes to turn her previous international experience into a stronger performance.

And Member Singi wants to transform the pain of losing a leg into the joy of winning a medal.

What they need most is an opportunity.

They have the ability to work hard. They have dreams. And they have the determination to represent Nepal.

The question now is not only how hard these four athletes are willing to work, but also how much support the state and sporting authorities are willing to provide.

Their story carries a simple message: physical limitations do not have to limit dreams. But turning those dreams into international medals requires opportunity, investment and support.

काठमांडू : हेलबा लेल पानि चाही, मुदा पैरा तैराक लेल पूल मे घुसब त शुरुआत मात्र अछि।

नियमित प्रशिक्षण, सुलभ बुनियादी ढाँचा, योग्य कोच, फिजियोथेरेपी, रिकवरी सुविधा, पोषण, परिवहन आ आर्थिक सहायता ओतबे महत्वपूर्ण छै.

नेपाल केरऽ पैरा तैराक, हालांकि, ऐन्हऽ बहुत सारा बुनियादी सुविधा के कमी के बीच अंतरराष्ट्रीय प्रतियोगिता के तैयारी करी रहलऽ छै । सीमित संसाधन आ कठिन परिस्थिति के बावजूद आगामी पैरा एशियाई खेल मे नेपाल के झंडा ऊँच फहराबय के सपना ल क प्रशिक्षण ल रहल छथिन्ह.

नेपाल २०१० सँ पारा एशियन खेलमे भाग लैत आबि रहल अछि ।मुदा महाद्वीपीय आयोजनमे ओकर उपलब्धि सीमित अछि ।

अब तलक नेपाल न॑ पैरा एशियाई खेलऽ म॑ खाली एगो पदक जीती चुकलऽ छै — जेकरा २०२३ म॑ १९वां एशियाई पैरा गेम्स म॑ ५६ किलोग्राम स॑ कम उम्र के वर्ग म॑ ताइक्वांडो एथलीट पलेशा गोवर्धन न॑ कांस्य पदक जीतल॑ छेलै ।

नेपाल के पैरा तैराकी टीम के आब उम्मीद अछि जे ओहि इतिहास मे एकटा नव अध्याय जोड़ल जाएत.

चुनौती के बावजूद प्रशिक्षण जारी अछि

नेपाल पारा तैराकी संघ के अन्तर्गत मुख्य प्रशिक्षक सुबास श्रेष्ठ चारिटा एथलीट — सृजना सरकी, जेनिशा कथायत, हरकमन घरती आ सदस्य सिंगबो के नियमित प्रशिक्षण दैत आबि रहल अछि ।

पिछला पांच स छह मास स एथलीट नियमित रूप स प्रशिक्षण ल रहल छथि।

कोच श्रेष्ठ के अनुसार प्रशिक्षण के दौरान एथलीट सब नीक प्रतिबद्धता देखौलक अछि। मुदा संसाधन आ सुविधा के कमी के कारण हुनकर तैयारी के वांछित स्तर पर पहुंचाबय मे दिक्कत भ गेल अछि.

स्विमिंग पूल तक पहुंच स्वयं एकटा पैघ चुनौती रहल छल। रिफ्रेश रिक्रिएशन सेंटर न॑ अपनऽ स्विमिंग पूल आरू लेन क॑ रियायती दर प॑ उपलब्ध कराय देला के बाद प्रशिक्षण कुछ आसान होय ​​गेलऽ छै ।

मुदा चुनौती पूल स आगू बढ़ि गेल अछि।

एथलीटऽ लेली फिजियोथेरेपी, रिकवरी सुविधा, जकूजी सेवा, पोषण, परिवहन आरू विशेष खेल उपकरण के व्यवस्था करना मुश्किल बनलऽ छै ।

श्रेष्ठ के लेलऽ सबसें बड़ऽ चुनौती सीमित संसाधन के साथ अंतरराष्ट्रीय स्तर के प्रतियोगिता लेली एथलीटऽ क॑ तैयार करना छै ।

हुनकऽ कहना छै कि एथलीटऽ म॑ प्रतिभा आरू दृढ़ संकल्प छै, लेकिन अपर्याप्त सुविधा के वजह स॑ हुनका अपनऽ पूरा क्षमता के अनुसार तैयारी करना मुश्किल होय जाय छै ।

तइयो हुनकऽ आत्मविश्वास आरू प्रतिबद्धता टीम क॑ आगू बढ़ाबै के काम जारी छै ।

सृजन के पहिल अंतरराष्ट्रीय सपना

19 वर्षीय सृजना सरकी लेल तैराकी खेल स बेसी अछि। ई अपना के साबित करय के तरीका सेहो अछि.

मूल रूप स कर्णाली प्रांत क जुमला क रहनिहार सरकी तीन साल पहिने माटि खोदैत काल भूस्खलन मे दफन भ गेलाक बाद अपन जीवन बदलि गेल छलीह। दुर्घटना के कारण हुनका विकलांगता के साथ रहय पड़लनि आ चुनौती के सिलसिला सेहो आबि गेलनि।

मुदा ओ अपन सपना सँ हार मानय सँ मना क देलनि।

वर्तमान में गोकर्णेश्वर में रहैत स्नातक के तैयारी में लागल सरकी नियमित रूप स अपन प्रशिक्षण स्थल पर जाइत छथि । कखनो टैक्सी त कखनो टेम्पो ल क अभ्यास तक पहुंचैत छथि ।

पिछला तीन मास स ओ तैराकी पर खास ध्यान द रहल छथि।

आगामी प्रतियोगिता हुनकऽ पहिलऽ अंतर्राष्ट्रीय आयोजन होतै ।

पहिल बेर नेपालक प्रतिनिधित्व करबाक अवसर पाबि उत्साहित छथि आ अपन क्षमताक अनुसार प्रदर्शन आ पदक लेल प्रतिस्पर्धा करबाक लेल दृढ़ संकल्पित छथि ।

सरकी लेली खाली अंतरराष्ट्रीय प्रतियोगिता म॑ पहुँचना पहल॑ स॑ ही एगो बड़ऽ उपलब्धि छै ।

मुदा ओ अपना केँ सहभागिता धरि सीमित नहि राखय चाहैत छथि ।

जखन ओ पानि मे प्रवेश करैत छथि तऽ चाहैत छथि जे हुनकर क्षमता — अपन अतीतक पीड़ा सँ बेसी — हुनका परिभाषित करय ।

हरकमन : दुनू हाथ गमाबसँ लऽ कऽ हेलबामे पहिचान ताकब धरि

बागलुंग के 21 वर्षीय हरकमन घरती के कहानी सेहो असाधारण लचीलापन के कहानी अछि.

एगारह साल पहिने हुनकर गाम मे पहिल बेर बिजली जुटल छल। एहि क्रम मे घरती कए मेन इन्सुलेटर कए छुलाक बाद करंट लागि गेल।

दुर्घटनाक परिणामस्वरूप हुनक दुनू हाथक क्षति भेलनि ।

लेकिन शारीरिक नुकसान स॑ हुनकऽ खेल म॑ प्रतिस्पर्धा करै के संकल्प कम नै होलै ।

घरती पिछला छह साल स घरेलू खेल मे सक्रिय छथि आ आब हुनका उम्मीद अछि जे ओ तैराकी क माध्यम स अंतरराष्ट्रीय स्तर पर अपन क्षमता साबित करताह।

एक साल पहिने जापान मे इंटरनेशनल एथलीट लाइसेंस प्राप्त केने छलाह।

लेकिन हुनका जकूजी सेवा आरू फिजियोथेरेपी सहित आवश्यक रिकवरी सुविधा के कमी जारी छै ।

एहि सीमा क कारण घरती क कहब अछि जे ओ आगामी प्रतियोगिता मे पदक क गारंटी नहि द सकैत छथि।

हुनकऽ महत्वाकांक्षा, लेकिन एक पदक स॑ भी आगू बढ़ी गेलऽ छै ।

हुनी भविष्य मँ ओलंपिक आरू विश्व चैंपियनशिप केरौ आयोजन मँ भाग लेबै लेली आवश्यक अनुभव आरू योग्यता के मानक जमा करना चाहै छै ।

घरती के लेल तैराकी खाली प्रतिस्पर्धा के बात नै छै। अपन शर्त पर दुनिया स परिचय कराबय के तरीका बनि गेल अछि.

जेनिशा के एकटा आओर मौका भेटैत छैक

सुदुरपश्चिम प्रांत के जेनिशा कथायत के लेल तैराकी कोनो नव यात्रा नै छै।

नौ साल स एहि खेल स जुड़ल छथि।

दसम कक्षा मे पढ़ैत काल हुनकर एकटा टांग छूटि गेलनि। तैयो ओ हेलब नहि छोड़लीह। बल्कि चुनौती क॑ प्रेरणा म॑ बदली क॑ खेल क॑ अपनऽ पहचान के हिस्सा बनैलकै ।

चीनमे आयोजित १९म एशियन खेलमे नेपालक प्रतिनिधित्व कठायत कऽ चुकल अछि ।

आयोजन मे जे प्रस्तुति आशा केने छलीह से नहि द सकलीह, मुदा अनुभव हुनकर आत्मविश्वास कमजोर नहि केलक।

बल्कि नीक तैयारी कए घुरबाक संकल्प कए मजबूत केलक।

उच्च शिक्षा जारी रखैत कथ्यत प्रशिक्षण पर सेहो अपन ध्यान बनौने रखने छथि ।

एहि बेर ओ अपन पिछला अंतरराष्ट्रीय अनुभव कए बेहतर प्रदर्शन मे बदलय चाहैत छथि।

ओकर लक्ष्य स्पष्ट छैक — पदक ।

सदस्य सिंगी : दुर्घटना स स्विमिंग लेन तक

चारो एथलीटऽ म॑ सदस्य सिंगी स्यांगबो केरऽ सड़क दुर्घटना स॑ ल॑ क॑ स्विमिंग पूल तक के यात्रा भी ओतने उल्लेखनीय छै ।

17 वर्षक उम्र मे स्यांगबो चीनक संग रसुवागढ़ी सीमाक समीप सड़क दुर्घटना मे पड़ि गेल छल।

ओ नेपाली कंटेनर ट्रक मे हेल्पर के काज करैत आबि रहल छलाह आ गाड़ी चलाबय सीखैत आ अनुभव प्राप्त करैत चीन गेल छलाह.

सीमा पर अपन बारीक प्रतीक्षा मे अचानक एकटा आओर गाड़ी हुनका टक्कर मारि देलक।

दुर्घटना मे हुनकर एकटा टांग छूटि गेलनि।

दुर्घटनाक बाद जीवन सहज नहि छल।

मुदा कृत्रिम पैरक व्यवस्था करैत काल स्यांगबो हेलबाक संपर्क मे आबि गेलाह ।

कहियो तैराक बनबाक योजना नहि बनौने छलाह ।

मौका भेटलाक बाद ओ एक बेर कोशिश करबाक विचार सँ बेसी किछु नहि ल' क' पोखरि मे प्रवेश केलनि.

धीरे-धीरे तैराकी हुनक जीवनक एकटा महत्वपूर्ण अंग बनि गेलनि ।

आब 26 वर्षीय स्यांगबो सब दिन ट्रेनिंग करैत अछि। करीब दू मास स नियमित प्रशिक्षण ल रहल छथि आ कहैत छथि जे हुनकर तैयारी नीक स आगू बढ़ि रहल अछि।

तैराकी आब खाली समय बिताबय के तरीका नहिं रहि गेल अछि.

प्रतिस्पर्धा शुरू केलाक बाद हुनकर महत्वाकांक्षा बदलि गेलनि।

“घर मे मेडल आनब” आब हुनकर स्पष्ट उद्देश्य अछि ।

स्यांगबो के मानना ​​छै कि नेपाल क॑ ई बार पैरा तैराकी म॑ पदक जीतै के अच्छा मौका छै आरू वू लक्ष्य के साथ प्रशिक्षण जारी रखै छै ।

हालांकि संबंधित संस्था सब प्रशिक्षण आ दैनिक खर्च मे किछु सहयोग देलक अछि, मुदा हुनकर कहब अछि जे उच्च स्तरीय तैयारी लेल जेतना सुविधा आवश्यक अछि ओ सब उपलब्ध नहि अछि।

हुनकर आत्मविश्वास, तथापि, मजबूत बनल अछि।

चारि टा एथलीट, एक गोल

सृजना अपन पहिल अंतरराष्ट्रीय प्रतियोगिता क तैयारी मे छथि।

जेनिशा अपनऽ पिछला अंतरराष्ट्रीय प्रदर्शन म॑ सुधार करना चाहै छै ।

हरकमन केरऽ नजर भविष्य केरऽ ओलंपिक आरू विश्व चैंपियनशिप लेली क्वालीफाइंग मार्ग प॑ छै ।

सदस्य सिंगी अपनऽ पहलऽ बड़ऽ अंतर्राष्ट्रीय अवसर प॑ पदक जीतना चाहै छै ।

हुनका लोकनिक कथा अलग-अलग अछि।

एकटा भूस्खलन के बाद विकलांग भ गेल। दोसर के बिजली दुर्घटना में दुनु हाथ गंवा गेल। दोसर के किशोरावस्था मे पैर गंवा देलक। चारिम के सड़क दुर्घटना मे पैर गंवा देल गेल।

मुदा दुनू गोटेक एकटा बात छनि — प्रतिस्पर्धा करबाक अटूट संकल्प ।

हुनकर सबस पैघ चुनौती सुविधा क कमी अछि।

सीमित फंडिंग, अपर्याप्त सुलभ खेल बुनियादी ढाँचा आ फिजियोथेरेपी, रिकवरी सुविधाक, उपकरण आ पोषण कें अपर्याप्त पहुंच छै.

प्रशिक्षण स्थल पर पहुंचय लेल सेहो व्यक्तिगत संघर्ष के जरूरत पड़ि सकैत अछि.

तइयो एक बेर पोखरि मे घुसि गेलाक बाद ओ कठिनाइ सभ अस्थायी रूप सँ एक कात धकेलि देल जाइत अछि ।

स्विमिंग लेन मे ओ अपन शारीरिक स्थिति सं बेसी अपन क्षमता पर ध्यान दैत छथिन्ह. हर स्ट्रोक हुनकऽ समय सुधारै के कोशिश छै, आरू हर प्रशिक्षण सत्र हुनका अंतरराष्ट्रीय मंच प॑ प्रदर्शन करै के सपना के करीब लानी दै छै ।

एकटा कोच’क चुनौती

मुख्य कोच सुबास श्रेष्ठ के लेल ई चारू एथलीट मात्र प्रतियोगी नै छैथ। ई सब महत्वपूर्ण क्षमता वाला एथलीट छैथ।

हुनकऽ दृढ़ संकल्प आरू कार्य नैतिकता मजबूत छै, लेकिन अंतरराष्ट्रीय स्तर प॑ प्रतिस्पर्धा करै लेली नियमित आरू वैज्ञानिक प्रशिक्षण के जरूरत छै ।

जेकरा लेल समय, उपकरण, सुविधा आ आर्थिक संसाधन चाही।

सीमित संसाधन वाला एथलीट क॑ तैयार करना श्रेष्ठ लेली एगो बड़ऽ चुनौती बनलऽ छै, लेकिन ओकरऽ क्षमता ओकरा प्रेरित करै के काम जारी छै ।

हुनकऽ दृष्टिकोण छै कि एथलीटऽ के सीमा के बजाय ओकरऽ क्षमता प॑ ध्यान केंद्रित करलऽ जाय, उपलब्ध संसाधनऽ के बेहतरीन संभव उपयोग करी क॑ ओकरऽ तकनीक, समय आरू प्रदर्शन म॑ सुधार करलऽ जाय ।

मुदा, नेपाल जँ अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय पदककेँ लक्षित करय चाहैत अछि तऽ ओकर तैयारी बेसी व्यवस्थित आ दीर्घकालीन बनेबाक आवश्यकता अछि, हुनकर मानब छनि ।

पानि मे सपना

नेपाल के पैरा-स्पोर्ट्स क्षेत्र मे एखन बहुत रास रास्ता तय करय के अछि.

एकटा पदक खेलक परिदृश्य कए नहि बदलि सकैत अछि। एथलीट कें लेल निरंतर निवेश, बुनियादी ढाँचा, प्रशिक्षण आ दीर्घकालिक सहायता आवश्यक छै.

फिलहाल चारिटा एथलीट स्विमिंग पूल मे अपन भविष्य क तलाश मे छथि।

सृजना अपन पहिल अंतरराष्ट्रीय यात्रा पर अपना कए साबित करय चाहैत छथि।

हरकमन अपनऽ खेल कैरियर क॑ ओलंपिक आरू विश्व चैंपियनशिप के तरफ ले जाय चाहै छै ।

जेनिशा क॑ उम्मीद छै कि वू अपनऽ पिछला अंतरराष्ट्रीय अनुभव क॑ मजबूत प्रदर्शन म॑ बदली देतै ।

आरू सदस्य सिंगी पैर खोबै के दर्द क॑ पदक जीतै के खुशी म॑ बदलना चाहै छै ।

हुनका सभकेँ सभसँ बेसी जरूरत अछि अवसर।

मेहनत करबाक क्षमता छनि। सपना होइत छनि। आ नेपालक प्रतिनिधित्व करबाक संकल्प हिनका लोकनिक अछि ।

आब सवाल ई छै कि ई चारो एथलीट कतेक मेहनत करै लेली तैयार छै, बल्कि ई भी छै कि राज्य आरू खेल प्राधिकारी कतेक सहयोग दै लेली तैयार छै ।

हुनकऽ कहानी म॑ एगो सरल संदेश छै कि शारीरिक सीमा के सपना क॑ सीमित करै के जरूरत नै छै । लेकिन वू सपना क॑ अंतरराष्ट्रीय पदक म॑ बदलै लेली अवसर, निवेश आरू सहयोग के जरूरत छै ।

full_article:
Nepal have handed the ODI captaincy back to experienced leg-spinner Sandeep Lamichhane ahead of the ACC Men’s Premier Cup in Malaysia, replacing Rohit Paudel.

The 26-year-old has previously led Nepal in 14 ODIs and returns to the role after Paudel took over in 2022.

googletag.cmd.push(function() { googletag.display('div-gpt-story-2'); });

Lamichhane has established himself as one of Nepal’s leading bowlers, reaching 150 ODI wickets faster than any other Nepalese player. He also became the first Nepal player to claim 100 wickets in T20 internationals.

Paudel enjoyed a successful spell as captain, guiding Nepal to 11 victories in 12 matches during the ICC Cricket World Cup League 2 campaign and helping them secure a place in the 2023 World Cup Qualifier in Zimbabwe.

The Premier Cup will take place from August 30 to September 12, with Nepal aiming to make an impact under their returning captain.

Nepal’s squad

Sandeep Lamichhane (captain), Rohit Paudel, Aasif Sheikh, Arjun Kumal, Dev Khanal, Dipendra Singh Airee, Basir Ahamad, Ishan Pandey, Gulshan Kumar Jha, Sher Malla, Lalit Narayan Rajbanshi, Karan KC, Hemant Dhami and Sundeep Jora.
translated:
नेपाल न॑ मलेशिया म॑ होबै वाला एसीसी पुरुष प्रीमियर कप स॑ पहल॑ रोहित पौडेल के जगह प॑ एकदिवसीय कप्तान पद अनुभवी लेग स्पिनर संदीप लामिछाने क॑ वापस सौंपलकै ।

26 वर्षीय खिलाड़ी एहि सं पहिने 14 एकदिवसीय मैच मे नेपाल के नेतृत्व केने छथिन्ह आओर 2022 मे पौडेल के पदभार संभालला के बाद फेर सं एहि भूमिका मे आबि रहल छथिन्ह.

लामिछाने नेपाल केरऽ प्रमुख गेंदबाजऽ म॑ स॑ एक के रूप म॑ खुद क॑ स्थापित करी क॑ एकदिवसीय कोनो भी अन्य खिलाड़ी स॑ भी तेजी स॑ १५० एकदिवसीय विकेट तक पहुँची गेलऽ छै । ओ टी-२० अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय मे १०० विकेट लेनिहार पहिल नेपाल खिलाड़ी सेहो बनल छल ।

पौडेल न॑ कप्तान के रूप म॑ सफल समय के आनंद लेलकै, जेकरा म॑ नेपाल क॑ आईसीसी क्रिकेट विश्व कप लीग २ अभियान के दौरान १२ मैचऽ म॑ ११ जीत के मार्गदर्शन करलकै आरू जिम्बाब्वे म॑ आयोजित २०२३ विश्व कप क्वालीफायर म॑ जगह पक्का करै म॑ मदद करलकै ।

प्रीमियर कप ३० अगस्त सँ १२ सितम्बर धरि होयत, जाहि मे नेपाल अपन वापसी करय बला कप्तान के नेतृत्व मे प्रभाव डालबाक लक्ष्य रखने अछि ।

title: Nepal Expresses Deep Sorrow Over Colombia Earthquake - Ratopati
description: Nepal Expresses Deep Sorrow Over Colombia Earthquake  Ratopati
publisher.title: Ratopati
full_article:
Kathmandu. The Government of Nepal has expressed deep sorrow over the human and physical damage caused by the powerful earthquake in the western part of Colombia.

Issuing a press note today, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs has expressed sympathy on behalf of the Government and people of Nepal to the Government and people of Colombia, offering condolences to those who lost their lives in the earthquake and heartfelt sympathy to the bereaved families.

The Ministry of Foreign Affairs said, "In this difficult situation, the Government and people of Nepal stand firmly with the Government and people of Colombia." The Government of Nepal has wished for the swift and successful rescue of those missing due to the earthquake.
